title: Restock Explorer

budget_curve.kind: Simulated: each policy's plan at every solved budget, valued on the 1,000 evaluation scenarios; the dashed line is the optimizer's in-sample value and the band its out-of-sample p10 to p90.
budget_curve.lie: A budget between two solved points was never solved, so the slider snaps instead of interpolating; the in-sample line never falls as the budget grows (test, within mip_gap x |bound|), but out-of-sample has no such guarantee and is shown as computed.
budget_curve.question: How much profit does each budget buy, and where does the optimizer's lead open or close?

buy_list.kind: Modelled: the stored plan at this budget; spend = units x unit cost, and the price is the chosen level's shelf price against today's.
buy_list.lie: Spend must stay within the budget and every listed price is a level the model kept (tests); costs and demand are synthetic, so this demonstrates the method, it is not a shopping list for a real store.
buy_list.question: What exactly should the shop buy at this budget, and which prices move?

curse_gap.kind: Simulated: in-sample objective on the 24 training scenarios minus the same plan's value on the 1,000 evaluation scenarios.
curse_gap.lie: Out-of-sample has no sign guarantee, so the gap is reported, never asserted; with 24 scenarios seed noise is large (EXPERIMENTS.md §5).
curse_gap.question: How much does the in-sample number flatter itself?

evpi_vss.kind: Modelled, in-sample: EEV (the average-scenario plan re-valued on the scenarios) <= RP (the stochastic plan) <= WS (perfect foresight per scenario); VSS = RP - EEV and EVPI = WS - RP.
evpi_vss.lie: Both are in-sample on the pinned 24 scenarios, not out-of-sample guarantees; a solve stopped short of its gap could break the order, so a test asserts EEV <= RP <= WS within the gap.
evpi_vss.question: Is planning for uncertainty worth it, and how much could perfect forecasts add?

fair_baseline.kind: Modelled: today's prices held fixed (ratio 1.00) while the buys are re-optimized by the same MILP, so the only thing it lacks is price choice.
fair_baseline.lie: A same-buys-at-today's-prices row would be a straw man; this row re-optimizes the buys (test: it equals the price-edit limit P = 0 rung within the gap).
fair_baseline.question: Is the lift just repricing, or does planning the buys matter too?

hull_bigm.kind: Counted: wall-clock seconds and termination status per solve, on identical instances with the same rel gap and a 120 s limit.
hull_bigm.lie: Timings depend on the machine and the HiGHS version (one recorded run); the result column records whether each solve reached the gap, so a timeout is never shown as optimal.
hull_bigm.question: Does the weekly tool solve fast enough to trust its answer?

rord.kind: Simulated: each policy's plan is valued on 1,000 fresh scenarios (eval seed 999) from the model's own demand generator, minus the same policy's budget-0 plan, divided by what it spent.
rord.lie: It flatters the optimizer if the evaluation set leaks into training (test: eval seed 999 is never a training seed) and it is only as true as the generator, so it is out-of-sample on the model's own generator, not on a real store.
rord.question: What does each restock dollar return, on demand the plan never saw?

saa.kind: Simulated: for N = 20 to 160 training scenarios, 10 seeds each, the plan's in-sample objective against its value on the 1,000 evaluation scenarios.
saa.lie: The gap shrinks with N on average but not at every step, and one seed can sit above or below the seed mean (EXPERIMENTS.md §5 prints the spread); the evaluation seed is never a training seed (test).
saa.question: Are 24 training scenarios enough?
